results.title: Emergency + real-time + signed pub/sub (LIFE-SAFETY — highest bar)

assessment.domain: Emergency + real-time + signed pub/sub (life-safety) — Surfaces 1 & 16 (audit immutability)
assessment.coverageNote: Traced end-to-end on master a8959842 (re-resolved every symbol, did not trust stale audit line numbers). Covered: emergency.controller.ts (trigger/all-clear/SOS/broadcast/media-alert/status/messages), screen-emergency.controller.ts (per-screen + bulk), redis.service.ts (fan-out gate, durable revocation), ws-signature.ts (verifyWsHmac), websocket-signer.service.ts, realtime.gateway.ts, sse.controller.ts + sse.service.ts, jwt-auth.guard.ts, rbac.guard.ts, panic-bypass.decorator.ts, users.controller.ts (canTriggerPanic staleness), screens.controller.ts manifest backstop + manifest-hot-cache.ts, required-secret.ts, audit-immutability migrations, and player emergency surfaces (player/page.tsx WS+SSE gates, panic/page.tsx hold-to-trigger). Verified forgery/replay/stale/wrong-scope cannot trigger or clear an alert, every trigger/clear writes an immutable audit row atomically, all-clear restores across all three scopes, and the manifest emergency field is the same Tenant.emergencyStatus + ScreenEmergencyOverride source of truth. Could not curl a live prod health endpoint (the Railway URL I tried 404'd at the edge — no prod URL supplied); all findings are code-verified. Net: this surface is genuinely well-hardened; no code BLOCKER found.

findings.title: Server-side forgery gate verifies HMAC before any fan-out (verifyWsHmac at Redis pmessage)
findings.evidence: redis.service.ts:191 calls verifyWsHmac(parsed, this.deviceSecret) inside handleRedisMessage BEFORE `this.gateway.broadcastToScope` (202) and `this.sse.broadcastToScope` (203); a failing verdict returns early (192-198). ws-signature.ts:51-91 recomputes the canonical string, does a length-checked crypto.timingSafeEqual, and enforces a ±120s freshness window. The dev/local-Redis fallback path also routes through the same handleRedisMessage (redis.service.ts:216), so there is no unverified publish path. realtime.module.ts:30 wires SSE into the same single verified subscriber.
findings.whatBreaks: A forged message published directly onto a tenant:*/group:*/device:* Redis channel (e.g. compromised Redis) is dropped server-side and never reaches a screen — it cannot trigger or clear a lockdown.

findings.title: AuditLog immutability is enforced at the storage layer (real triggers), and the 3-trigger duplication that 500'd user deletes was resolved
findings.evidence: Migration 20260531000000_audit_logs_immutable installs audit_logs_immutable BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE, blocking all DELETEs and all content UPDATEs while permitting only the FK user_id->NULL anonymization (byte-identical otherwise). Migration 20260609000000_dedupe_audit_immutability_triggers drops the older blanket audit_log_immutable_no_update/no_delete pair that otherwise fired first and broke user deletion, and re-asserts the smart trigger idempotently. Storage-layer append-only guarantee is intact.
findings.whatBreaks: A compromised API process or direct-DB actor cannot tamper with or delete emergency trigger/clear history; forensic trail survives even user deletion.

findings.title: Every trigger and clear writes an immutable audit row atomically with the state mutation
findings.evidence: Tenant trigger wraps Tenant.update + auditLog.create + per-screen upserts in one $transaction (emergency.controller.ts:488-517); group/device trigger wraps audit + overrideUpserts (546-564). All-clear wraps clear + deleteMany + audit per scope (673-695 tenant, 703-717 device, 729-747 group). SOS/broadcast/media-alert each wrap message + audit (871, 961, 1042). Per-screen controller wraps upsert+audit and delete+audit, surfacing a 500 (not silent success) if the audit write fails (screen-emergency.controller.ts:255-326, 431-462).
findings.whatBreaks: No half-committed state where emergencyStatus flips without an audit row (or vice versa); a failed audit write rolls back the trigger rather than lying 'triggered'.

findings.title: All-clear reliably restores across tenant/group/device scopes; player treats the authenticated manifest as the sole arbiter so a forged ALL_CLEAR cannot cancel a real alert
findings.evidence: Tenant all-clear sets emergencyStatus=INACTIVE, nulls both playlist pointers, and deletes ALL screenEmergencyOverride rows for the tenant (emergency.controller.ts:673-684); device + group all-clear delete the per-screen override rows so a rebooted poll-only kiosk drops lockdown (696-748) — the emergency-003 fix. Player: WS ALL_CLEAR is intentionally NOT optimistic — it only calls fetchContent(), and the manifest re-fetch clears the overlay only if Tenant.emergencyStatus reports cleared (player/page.tsx:4360-4374, 4396-4398). ALL_CLEAR_MESSAGE clears pushed overlays on both WS (4199) and SSE (4199 handler) tiers.
findings.whatBreaks: Operator hits All Clear and every screen (incl. rebooted, poll-only, WS-blocked-proxy) drops the alert; a spoofed ALL_CLEAR cannot drop a genuine lockdown because the re-fetch re-asserts server state.

findings.title: canTriggerPanic staleness is closed — removing the capability revokes the user's live tokens
findings.evidence: RbacGuard reads the JWT claim typedUser.canTriggerPanic (rbac.guard.ts:71) for @AllowPanicBypass. On a true->false transition users.controller.ts:430-432 calls revokeUserTokens -> redis.markUserTokensInvalid, which writes a per-user invalid-before epoch (redis.service.ts:314-335) mirrored durably to Postgres. jwt-auth.guard.ts:113-118 rejects any user token whose iat predates that epoch, failing CLOSED on Redis error (119-126). RESTRICTED_VIEWER can never bypass even if the flag is set (rbac.guard.ts:69-73, writer refuses at users.controller.ts:387-392).
findings.whatBreaks: A receptionist/guard whose panic capability is revoked can no longer fire /emergency/trigger via the stale 30-day JWT claim — their outstanding tokens are invalidated immediately.

findings.title: Manifest HTTP-poll backstop reads the same source of truth and covers group/device scope
findings.evidence: getManifest computes emergencyActiveForThisScreen = !!activeScreenOverride || tenant.emergencyStatus !== 'INACTIVE' (screens.controller.ts:2605-2607), reading the identical Tenant.emergencyStatus + ScreenEmergencyOverride rows the trigger writes. Group/device triggers explicitly persist per-screen overrides (emergency.controller.ts:518-564) so a WS+SSE-blocked kiosk still sees the alert on its next poll. Cross-tenant manifest read is blocked (device token must match screen.id; user token tenant must match — 2519-2533). Hot-cache is 2s TTL and explicitly invalidated on trigger/clear (575, 752).
findings.whatBreaks: The most-degraded screen (both realtime transports blocked) still gets the lockdown within the ~10s poll window; no scope silently misses.

findings.title: Hold-to-trigger UX, cross-tenant scope authorization, and player replay/freshness/dedup gate all intact
findings.evidence: panic/page.tsx:37 HOLD_DURATION_MS=3000 with progress ring + aria-live announcements (196, 253). resolveScopeTenant re-resolves the owning tenant from ScreenGroup/Screen and 403s cross-tenant non-supers before any mutation (emergency.controller.ts:267-317); playlistId is verified to belong to the scope tenant (376-386, screen-emergency 374-390, bulk 543-563). Player SENSITIVE_TYPES gate requires a signature field, enforces a 30s clock-offset-adjusted freshness window, and dedups eventIds with a bounded LRU (player/page.tsx:4325-4358).
findings.whatBreaks: Accidental taps, cross-tenant triggers, and replayed sensitive events are all prevented; nothing regressed here.

findings.title: Player-side end-to-end signature verification (Ed25519) is not implemented — player only checks that a signature field is PRESENT
findings.evidence: player/page.tsx:4334 drops sensitive events with no signature field but does NOT cryptographically verify it (comment 4294-4306: 'we don't verify it here'; full asymmetric verify is a documented follow-up). ws-signature.ts:12-18 and websocket-signer.service.ts:38-55 confirm the HMAC secret is deliberately never shipped to kiosks and the ed25519 path (ws-ed25519.ts) is referenced but not wired to the player.
findings.whatBreaks: The server-side HMAC gate (Finding 1) is the real defense and blocks forged messages before they reach any player; residual exposure is only a compromised API replica or an attacker positioned between the verified gate and the TLS-protected socket. Genuine multi-week hardening (per-tenant key issuance at pair time), not a days-away launch item.

findings.title: SSE stream re-checks token revocation only at open — an already-open stream keeps delivering after a device token is revoked / screen unpaired
findings.evidence: sse.controller.ts:69-76 checks jwt_revoked_list once at stream open and resolves tenantId/groupId from the live Screen row at open (81-95), then hands off to a long-lived stream (128) with no periodic revocation or screen-status re-check. Contrast: the manifest poll re-reads screen.status===REVOKED every request (screens.controller.ts:2492) and the WS gateway re-validates on each (re)connect (realtime.gateway.ts:135-159). Token also travels in the query string (documented tradeoff, sse.controller.ts:19-27).
findings.whatBreaks: After an admin revokes a compromised device token (or unpairs/re-tenants the screen), that screen's currently-open SSE connection continues receiving its previously-resolved tenant/scope emergency events until the stream naturally drops or reconnects. Low severity: re-pair emits TENANT_CHANGED which wipes the token and forces reconnect, and EventSource reconnects on error; exposure is a bounded window, not indefinite in practice.
findings.fixSketch: In SseService.register, periodically (e.g. on each keepalive tick) re-run redis.sismember('jwt_revoked_list', token) and re-read screen.status; close the stream on revoked/REVOKED. Or cap SSE lifetime with a short max-age forcing a full re-auth.

findings.title: The HMAC gate's entire security rests on DEVICE_SECRET_KEY / DEVICE_JWT_SECRET secrecy — rotation (W0-01) is still human-gated
findings.evidence: requireSecret refuses production boot if these are unset/short (required-secret.ts:30-40), so there is no default-secret boot. But the signer (websocket-signer.service.ts:59) and the fan-out verifier (redis.service.ts:69) share DEVICE_SECRET_KEY, and the device-JWT verify uses DEVICE_JWT_SECRET (realtime.gateway.ts:123, jwt-auth.guard.ts:78). If either value was ever committed/exposed historically, an attacker could mint valid HMAC signatures that PASS the gate in Finding 1. MEMORY + task list confirm W0-01 secret ROTATION on Railway env is still open/Greg-gated.
findings.whatBreaks: Only a decision/secret action, not code: rotate DEVICE_SECRET_KEY, DEVICE_JWT_SECRET, JWT_SECRET, SESSION_SECRET to fresh crypto-random values in the production (Railway) env before public launch. verdict.reasoning: Independently traced the full chain on master and every cited line matches. rbac.guard.ts:69-73 gates @AllowPanicBypass on the JWT claim typedUser.canTriggerPanic AND role!==RESTRICTED_VIEWER. users.controller.ts:430-432 calls revokeUserTokens ONLY on a true->false transition; revokeUserTokens->markUserTokensInvalid (redis.service.ts:314-335) writes a per-user invalid-before epoch (+1s to catch same-second tokens) and mirrors it to Postgres FIRST (line 324) before the throwing Redis SET. jwt-auth.guard.ts:113-118 rejects any non-device user token with payload.iat < invalidBefore, and 119-126 fails CLOSED on Redis error. getTokenInvalidBefore (redis.service.ts:450-472) falls back to the durable Postgres store on Redis failure and still fails closed on a total outage. Attempted refutation: revokeUserTokens swallows markUserTokensInvalid errors (warn, no rethrow), but the durable mirror is written before the throwing Redis call and the DB row canTriggerPanic=false is already committed in the transaction, so revocation persists via Postgres even with Redis down; only a simultaneous Redis+Postgres write-time outage lets a stale token live to its own expiry — an acceptable documented degradation, not a bypass. The claim (staleness is closed) is accurate; there is no launch-blocking defect. Set severity LOW because this is a verified-safe control, not a vulnerability.

results.title: Auth, identity, tenant isolation, session store

assessment.domain: Auth, identity, tenant isolation, session store (Standard Audit Surface §10 + §16)
assessment.coverageNote: Audited current master HEAD a8959842. Traced end-to-end: JWT issuance/verification (jwt.strategy.ts, jwt-auth.guard.ts), single-token + per-user-epoch revocation (auth.controller logout, redis.service markUserTokensInvalid + durable RevokedCredential mirror), Argon2 login with timing-equalizer (auth.service.ts), express-session config (main.ts), RbacGuard role+tenant scope (rbac.guard.ts), and tenant-scoped CRUD across assets/playlists/schedules/users/emergency/sso/tenants/bugs controllers. Attempted a cross-tenant read/write trace on every core resource: all use check-then-act tenantId scoping (findFirst{id,tenantId} guard before the by-id mutation) — no concrete cross-tenant leak found. Confirmed SAML is honestly gated (passport-saml NOT installed, 503, SUPER_ADMIN-only enable, hard enabled-gate on the unauthenticated callback, 0 enabled tenants), OIDC lib (openid-client ^5.7.1) IS installed with state/nonce fail-closed. Verified tenant-switch authorization tree and SUPER_ADMIN-only role-change with same-tenant scope + downgrade revocation. NOT deep-audited: full MFA/TOTP enrollment cryptography (mfa-secret-cipher/totp.ts read only at the login-diversion level), and per-endpoint sweep of every one of ~55 controllers (spot-checked the sensitive ones). Could not run the app (read-only mandate) so revocation fail-closed behavior is verified by code-read, not live.

findings.title: JWT revocation is durable + fail-closed and actually wired on role downgrade

findings.title: express-session uses the default in-memory MemoryStore — not multi-replica safe, and a memory leak at scale
findings.evidence: main.ts:163-191 configures session() with NO `store:` option → express-session falls back to MemoryStore. railway.json numReplicas=1 (single replica today). The session is used ONLY by SSO OIDC state/nonce (sso.controller.ts:94-119 session.ssoOidcState/ssoOidcNonce). No RedisStore/connect-redis anywhere in apps/api/src.
findings.whatBreaks: Works today at 1 replica. The moment Railway scales to numReplicas>1, an OIDC login initiated on replica A stores state on that pod's heap; the IdP callback load-balanced to replica B finds no session → validateOidcCallback:401 throws 'missing state/nonce (expired session or possible CSRF)' and every SSO login fails intermittently. Independently, MemoryStore is documented by express-session as not-for-production (unbounded growth / leak). JWT/password auth is unaffected (Bearer header, not cookie-session), so only OIDC SSO is at risk — but that's the enterprise login path being sold.
findings.fixSketch: Back express-session with a Redis store (connect-redis on the existing RedisService client) so OIDC state/nonce is shared across replicas and bounded. Alternatively move OIDC state/nonce off session into a signed, short-TTL cookie or a Redis key keyed by state. Until then, keep numReplicas=1 (config-gated) and document that SSO breaks on horizontal scale.

findings.title: RbacGuard enforces tenant scope only when districtId/schoolId is an explicit request field — :id resource routes rely entirely on per-service discipline

results.title: Storage, content pipeline, USB, offline cache

assessment.domain: Storage, content pipeline, USB sneakernet, offline cache (Standard Audit Surface §2)
assessment.coverageNote: Covered on live master a8959842 (clean tree): Supabase storage service (buckets, Cache-Control/egress, floor-plan signing, presign+complete-upload, per-type caps, SVG block, delete); USB export controller vs the Android UsbIngester.kt/UsbCacheIndex.kt contract + the W0-04 cross-language spec; player service-worker offline tiers (sw-player.js emergency never-evict floor + copy-forward); asset hard-delete vs UI copy; null-hash acceptance; boot-time hash backfill. EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED against prod: queried prod Postgres (172 assets — 0 Supabase null-hash, all 22 videos hashed, 18 null-hash rows are all external URLs) and live-curled a presign-uploaded video on Supabase — served `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` with `cf-cache-status: MISS→HIT`, so the 98MB→5.79GB egress incident is genuinely fixed on BOTH the server-reupload and the browser-PUT presign paths. Could not drive an end-to-end USB ingest on a physical Android player (no device); USB findings are code+contract-verified, not device-verified. Prod API hostname in docs (api-production-39a1) not re-curled here; used the DB + Supabase CDN directly.

findings.title: USB export silently DROPS assets that have a null fileHash instead of hashing the bytes it already downloads
findings.evidence: apps/api/src/usb-export/usb-export.controller.ts:316-320 — `const hash = asset.fileHash?.trim(); if (!hash) { this.logger.warn('Skipping asset ... no fileHash'); continue; }`. The asset is then absent from the ZIP, from topLevelAssets[], and from the playlist items[]. The /assets presign upload path never sends a hash (apps/web/src/app/[schoolId]/assets/page.tsx:528-534 omits fileHash), so complete-upload stores fileHash=null (assets.controller.ts:670-672); healing depends on a best-effort boot backfill capped at 100/boot (maintenance/backfill-asset-hashes.ts:7, wired main.ts:332).
findings.whatBreaks: An operator who uploads content (esp. a large video via presign) and immediately builds a USB bundle gets a ZIP that silently omits that asset — no error is surfaced (server-side warn only; the response `truncated` flag is NOT set for this case). The playlist plays with missing items on the offline kiosk. Prod is currently NOT materialized (DB shows 0 Supabase null-hash — backfill kept up), so this is a fresh-upload-before-next-boot race, not an active outage.
findings.fixSketch: In processPlaylist, the loop already fetches every asset's bytes via safeFetch — compute sha256 of fetched.body there and use it (persist back to Asset.fileHash) instead of `continue`-ing on null. Removes the silent-drop entirely and closes the backfill race.

findings.title: USB `includeEmergency` bundles only the tenant-level emergencyPlaylistId, omitting the 6 per-screen per-type emergency playlists (lockdown/evacuate/weather/hold/secure/medical) + portrait variants
findings.evidence: apps/api/src/usb-export/usb-export.controller.ts:263-265 selects only `tenant.emergencyPlaylistId` (comment at :180-186 acknowledges the single-field limitation). But the schema stores per-type emergency playlists on the Screen model — packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:814-819 (emergencyLockdownPlaylistId … emergencyMedicalPlaylistId) + portrait variants :840-845, set via screens.controller.ts:2085-2090. A screen-scoped bundle (body.screenId present) never captures that screen's per-type emergency content.
findings.whatBreaks: A fully-offline school that relies on a pre-loaded USB bundle for life-safety content gets only the tenant-default emergency board on-device; the type-specific lockdown/evacuate/etc. boards a screen was configured with are not in the bundle. Degradation of the offline emergency path (network WS/polling is the primary trigger route, so narrow), but life-safety-adjacent and silent.
findings.fixSketch: When body.screenId is set, also read that Screen's emergency*PlaylistId (and portrait variants), dedupe with the tenant default, and include all resolvable ones in emergencyRaw; document that per-screen emergency content is bundled.

findings.title: Emergency-tier USB folder split is deferred: API writes ALL assets to assets/, never emergency/, so the Android player's emergencyCount is always 0
findings.evidence: usb-export.controller.ts:322 hardcodes `storagePath = assets/${hash}.${ext}` for emergency playlist assets too (processPlaylist runs for both playlistsRaw and emergencyRaw). The Android ingester distinguishes tier by prefix — UsbIngester.kt:116 `tier = if (localPath.startsWith("emergency/")) "emergency" else "playlist"` — and reports emergencyCount (UsbIngester.kt:146,159), which will therefore always be 0.
findings.whatBreaks: Only telemetry/status: the kiosk state.json under-reports emergency asset count. No functional loss — UsbCacheIndex is a permanent on-disk replica with NO eviction (UsbCacheIndex.kt has no evict path), so emergency assets still land on disk and resolve via url→file lookup and survive offline.
findings.fixSketch: Route assets that belong to emergencyPlaylists to `emergency/<hash>.<ext>` (write into a second JSZip folder + set localPath accordingly) so the ingester counts and can prioritize them.

findings.title: Asset delete removes the storage object BEFORE the DB delete transaction, so a tx failure leaves a row pointing at a 404'd file
findings.evidence: apps/api/src/assets/assets.controller.ts:1240-1250 — `this.storage.delete(storagePath)` (line 1242) runs, THEN `$transaction(tx.asset.delete + auditLog)` (line 1249). If the transaction throws, the object is already gone but the Asset row survives.
findings.whatBreaks: A rare partial-delete: the media library still lists the asset but its fileUrl 404s on screens/thumbnails. Storage delete failures are already swallowed (warn only), so the inverse (row deleted, file orphaned) is also possible but harmless. Low likelihood.
findings.fixSketch: Delete the DB row inside the transaction first, then delete the storage object after the tx commits (best-effort); orphaned storage bytes are recoverable by a sweep, a dangling row is not.

findings.title: Cache-Control / egress incident (98MB→5.79GB) — VERIFIED FIXED on both upload paths
findings.evidence: Live curl of a presign-uploaded prod video (bhdaxzfalaycfopvcopm.supabase.co/.../object/public/assets/e4f2de09.../bb1a51d3....mp4, which has processing_meta=null → no server re-upload, i.e. the raw browser-PUT object): `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, `cf-cache-status: MISS` then `HIT` on repeat. Server path sets the bare form (supabase-storage.service.ts:379); presign browser-PUT sets the full string (assets/page.tsx:513) — both are honored + CDN-cached. Optimized images re-upload via uploadToBucket (assets.controller.ts:767).
findings.whatBreaks: Nothing — objects are served immutable and edge-cached. NOTE: the storage-service comment (supabase-storage.service.ts:371-379) claiming the full-string form is silently downgraded to no-cache is stale/context-specific and contradicted by the live wire header; it's a foot-gun for a future dev but not a runtime bug.
findings.fixSketch: Reconcile the two contradictory Cache-Control comments (assets/page.tsx:505-513 vs supabase-storage.service.ts:371-379) to reflect the verified reality: both forms serve immutable.

findings.title: USB API↔Android bundle contract agrees (W0-04) and is locked by a cross-language spec
findings.evidence: API emits schema:'edu-cms-usb-bundle/v1', bundleVersion, flat assets[]{url,sha256,localPath,mimeType,sizeBytes} (usb-export.controller.ts:114,382-387,342-348). Android reads exactly those: UsbIngester.kt:95-96 gates schema, :101 reads assets[], :114-115 reads sha256/localPath, :134-136 re-hashes + rejects on mismatch; UsbCacheIndex.kt:54-71 maps url/sha256→localPath file. usb-bundle-contract.spec.ts pins both the manifest shape and the controller source literals. HMAC-signed manifest (usbIngestKey), ingest gated on usbIngestEnabled (:198), false PIN claim removed from README (:429-432).
findings.whatBreaks: Nothing — a bundle produced today is accepted and verified by the player; signature + per-asset sha256 both enforced.

findings.title: Player offline emergency tier is a genuine never-evict floor served ahead of playlist content
findings.evidence: apps/web/public/sw-player.js: EMERGENCY_CACHE is a separate cache (:64); playlist LRU eviction only touches PLAYLIST_CACHE (precachePlaylist :376-390) so it can never evict emergency assets; fetch handler tries emergency cache first (:277-278); SW upgrade copies old emergency+meta entries into the new versioned cache BEFORE deleting stale (:121-152); set-hash is committed only after every emergency asset is re-verified present in cache (:435-456). Emergency manifest ships sha256:fileHash??null and SW skips body-hash verification when null (documented, graceful) — backfill heals null hashes (0 Supabase null-hash in prod).
findings.whatBreaks: Nothing — emergency media survives SW upgrades and playlist churn and is served first. The 1GB EMERGENCY_FLOOR_BYTES is a reporting constant (:615), not an enforced quota, but the structural separation makes the tier effectively never-evicted (note: no navigator.storage.persist() call, so under extreme origin-wide storage pressure the browser could still evict — acceptable on a dedicated kiosk).

findings.title: Asset hard-delete is honest to the customer and guards life-safety playlists
findings.evidence: Delete is a true hard-delete (assets.controller.ts:1250 tx.asset.delete) with a forensic AuditLog capturing mime/size/hash/name (:1251-1266). UI copy consistently says 'will be permanently deleted' (assets/page.tsx:300,1122,1317,1575) — no recycle-bin/restore/undo promised anywhere. Delete is BLOCKED (409) if the asset is protected screen-emergency content (:1200-1207) or in a protected emergency playlist (:1224-1232), preventing silent emptying of life-safety playlists.
findings.whatBreaks: Nothing — no false recoverability promise; life-safety content cannot be deleted out from under an active emergency config.

findings.title: Floor-plan private bucket + short-TTL signed URLs with safe graceful degradation
findings.evidence: floor-plans bucket created public:false and re-asserted every boot (supabase-storage.service.ts:171-191); floor-plan reads re-sign via 15-min TTL (floor-plans.controller.ts:218,238-252). On signing failure the code falls back to the stored URL (:251) — for NEW plans (private bucket) that URL is not world-readable so it fails CLOSED (image just won't load, privacy preserved); only OLD plans already in the public assets bucket fall back to an already-public URL, i.e. no new exposure. RESTRICTED_VIEWER removed from read (:256-265).
findings.whatBreaks: Nothing that leaks — the 'fail-open' fallback cannot expose a private-bucket plan; it only degrades to what was already public for legacy rows.

findings.title: Sponsor proof-of-play cue-fired endpoint is public + tokenless — forgeable at thousands/hour despite mitigations

Mitigations are real: cueId validated against CTS_CINEMATIC_CUE_IDS ∪ per-sport keys ∪ custom (sports.service.ts:122-135), (cueId,team) dedup 2s (CTS_CUE_DEDUP_MS=2000), rate-limit 40/10s (FEED_WINDOW_MS=10000, FEED_MAX_PER_WINDOW=40). But 40 valid impressions/10s = ~14,400/hr, and ~40 catalog cueIds × 3 teams give ample distinct dedup slots, so anyone who knows a public game id can inject a large volume of *valid-id* impressions.

finding.title: Manually-pasted YouTube/Twitch/Vimeo streaming channels are unplayable — widget renders 'No channel selected' (the #1 marketed streaming path is broken end-to-end)
finding.evidence: apps/web/.../settings/streaming/page.tsx:770 stores iframe channels as `playbackUrl: playbackType === 'iframe' ? undefined : manualUrl` — the real URL lives ONLY in externalId. streaming.service.ts:290 resolvePlayback returns `playbackUrl: ch.playbackUrl` (null) and never returns externalId; listChannels DTO maps `playbackUrl: c.playbackUrl || undefined`. PropertiesPanel.tsx:5064-5066 picker copies `playbackUrl: channel.playbackUrl` and `embedUrl: channel.playbackType==='iframe' ? channel.playbackUrl : undefined` — both undefined. StreamingWidget.tsx:124 then hits `if (!c.playbackUrl && !c.embedUrl)` → renders the '📺 No channel selected — Connect a streaming provider' empty state.
finding.whatBreaks: An operator follows the heavily-marketed flow (settings/streaming/page.tsx:202 'Any public YouTube channel or live stream. Paste the URL, that's it.'; streaming.service.ts:339 calls YouTube 'the signage operator's #1 source'), connects an iframe provider, pastes a YouTube/Twitch/Vimeo URL, picks that channel on a template — and the screen shows an empty 'No channel selected' card instead of the stream. Preset public-broadcaster channels and custom-HLS (.m3u8) channels work (they persist the URL into playbackUrl); ONLY the manual iframe-URL paste — the primary advertised path for the #1 source — is broken.
finding.fixSketch: Either persist the URL into playbackUrl for iframe too (drop the `? undefined` at page.tsx:770), OR have resolvePlayback/listChannels fall back to externalId when playbackUrl is null, OR make the picker copy `embedUrl: channel.playbackType==='iframe' ? (channel.playbackUrl || channel.externalId) : undefined`. Any one closes it; add a regression test that a picked iframe channel yields a non-empty embedUrl.

verdict.reasoning: Traced the full chain on master and every cited line is accurate. settings/streaming/page.tsx:764-770 sets playbackType='iframe' for YouTube/Twitch/Vimeo and stores playbackUrl:undefined, leaving the real URL only in externalId (line 768). streaming.service.ts listChannels (line 216) returns playbackUrl:undefined for iframe rows (it does also return externalId+playbackType, but the picker ignores externalId). PropertiesPanel.tsx:5064-5066 copies playbackUrl:channel.playbackUrl (undefined) and embedUrl:channel.playbackType==='iframe'?channel.playbackUrl:undefined → both undefined; externalId is never mapped into the widget config. StreamingWidget.tsx:124 then hits `if(!c.playbackUrl && !c.embedUrl)` and renders the 'No channel selected' empty state. No runtime resolvePlayback/re-fetch by streamingChannelId recovers the URL, so the break is end-to-end. Scope is correctly limited: preset channels (page.tsx:808 stores p.embedUrl||p.playbackUrl) and custom-HLS (stores manualUrl) both work — only the manually-pasted iframe path, which the UI markets as the #1 source, is broken. Real functional break on the primary advertised streaming path, but it does not crash the app, lose data, or breach security, so HIGH/SHOULD_FIX is honest rather than a hard launch BLOCKER.

findings.title: Container CVE scan (Trivy) is non-blocking — a CRITICAL/HIGH OS or library CVE in the production image will not fail CI

findings.whatBreaks: A newly-disclosed CRITICAL CVE in node:20-alpine or a shipped npm lib lands in the production container and CI stays green; nobody is alerted from the pipeline. findings.fixSketch: Triage the current CRITICAL/HIGH backlog in one real CI run (the scan needs a Docker daemon, hence it was never verified locally), rebase the base image / add ignore entries for accepted-risk CVEs, then drop continue-on-error so a NEW critical CVE reds the build.

findings.title: DEVICE_JWT_SECRET is not validated at boot — contradicts the documented 'refuses to start if missing' guarantee
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md claims the API refuses to start in prod if any of JWT_SECRET/SESSION_SECRET/DEVICE_SECRET_KEY/DEVICE_JWT_SECRET is missing. But every DEVICE_JWT_SECRET requireSecret call is inside a METHOD body, never a class field / boot path: jwt-auth.guard.ts:78, screens.controller.ts:90/315, gpio.controller.ts:82, sse.controller.ts:55, realtime.gateway.ts:123, devices.controller.ts:110, player-logs.controller.ts:66. `grep 'private readonly.*DEVICE_JWT_SECRET'` → no matches. So it is validated lazily on first device-auth request, not at boot.
findings.whatBreaks: A prod deploy that sets the other three secrets but omits DEVICE_JWT_SECRET boots successfully, passes the Railway healthcheck (liveness doesn't touch device auth), and looks fully green — then every screen pairing / device-token verify / SSE / WS device connect throws 500 at runtime. The failure surfaces as 'screens can't connect,' far from the real cause. (Prod today has it set — devices work — so this is a latent env-misconfig trap, not a live outage.)
findings.fixSketch: Add DEVICE_JWT_SECRET (and any other lazily-checked required secret) to an explicit boot-time assertion in main.ts bootstrap, mirroring the ALLOWED_ORIGINS/connection_limit refuse-to-boot block, so the documented guarantee actually holds.

findings.title: uncaughtException / unhandledRejection handlers are log-only (no exit) — process can keep serving from a corrupted state
findings.evidence: main.ts:24-31 registers both handlers that only console.error and deliberately do NOT rethrow or process.exit ('we'd rather log than let Railway restart the container mid-demo'). Node's own guidance is that resuming after an uncaughtException leaves the process in an undefined state.
findings.whatBreaks: After a genuine uncaughtException the process stays alive and may serve responses from a half-broken state (leaked handles, partial writes) rather than being recycled by Railway's restart policy + always-200 liveness. This is a deliberate availability tradeoff appropriate for a controlled launch; hardening it (graceful drain-then-exit on uncaughtException, keep swallow on unhandledRejection) is a post-launch reliability item, not a days-away fix.
findings.fixSketch: Post-launch: on uncaughtException, log + attempt a graceful server.close() with a short timeout then process.exit(1), letting Railway's 10× restart policy recycle a clean pod; keep unhandledRejection log-only or convert to a tracked metric.

synthesis.overallVerdict: READY FOR CONTROLLED LAUNCH — 0 surviving code blockers; launch-gated only on Greg's config/secret actions plus a short truth-in-advertising fix list
synthesis.readinessSummary: The load-bearing surfaces are genuinely hardened, not theater. Emergency/real-time (server-side HMAC forgery gate before any fan-out, atomic immutable audit, manifest+per-screen all-clear across all three scopes, canTriggerPanic revocation, storage-layer append-only) all verified real. Auth/tenant isolation, the Stripe webhook (idempotent/out-of-order/SERIALIZABLE-safe), POS direct connectors, signed emergency webhooks with durable multi-replica retry, and the W0-09/AI-Designer containment fixes all held up under adversarial re-verification. Critically, the two findings originally rated BLOCKS_LAUNCH/HIGH — the stale /help/billing article and the broken manual-iframe streaming path — were both downgraded by verifiers to SHOULD_FIX: real defects, but neither is unsafe, data-lossy, nor breaks the primary signage/emergency job. So there are ZERO genuine code launch-blockers. The residual risk is concentrated in (a) Greg's config/secret actions (secret rotation, Resend domain, PILOT_SEAT_LIMIT, Stripe, POS OAuth) and (b) a cluster of truth-in-advertising dents — quarantined boards still reachable via the builder picker and the public homepage, streaming "paste the URL, that's it" showing an empty card, email silently dropping non-owner mail while reporting SENT. A controlled/limited-cohort launch in days is defensible once the config gating is done and the top truth dents are patched. It is not yet "world-class": accessibility backlog, structural tenant isolation, a template-release pipeline, and Taurus container-query debt are honest multi-week items.
